precepts.text: The acts of Solomon are also written in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer. There is a prophet called Ahijah that wrote books we know nothing about. Our forefathers in the time of the Greeks, Judas Maccabeus and the woman with the seven sons, were ready to die because they had a level of understanding from those other books; we are just starting to figure it out piece by piece today.
precepts.point: Is it that book you see they have out there on the Bible apps? Leave that alone. The books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat?” Nathan's book is another we are supposed to have. There is also a prophet called Ahijah who wrote books we know nothing about, and Iddo the seer, another prophet, another book.

Those prophets went into some heavy stuff. Ask yourself why, in the time of the Greeks, when Antiochus came against us, Judas Maccabeus, the woman with the seven sons and our forefathers thought the way they did. They were ready to die. Even that group that said, I'd rather die than fight on the Sabbath, just kill me, I'm going to die in my innocency. They had a level of understanding that they got from those seventy books. We are not learning about regeneration and certain things today, but they were far past that back then.

They understood things that we are just starting to figure out piece by piece today. That is why we will never say we understand everything or have one hundred percent truth: “now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” Our flesh cannot contain some of these things, and when Christ returns we will know.

precepts.text: The same yearly weight of gold coming to Solomon is recorded, showing this is the compressed retelling of the fuller history.
precepts.point: Solomon makes two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold and puts them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

precepts.why:
“Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred threescore and six talents of gold.” Kings records the same yearly weight of gold that Chronicles gives: six hundred sixty and six talents.

Chronicles is the compressed retelling of the fuller history in Kings. The same gold, beside what the merchants and the kings of Arabia and the governors brought, went into the two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold that Solomon put in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

points: The Queen of Sheba hears of the fame of Solomon in her own land and travels to Jerusalem to prove him, meaning to test him, with hard questions from what she has heard.
She comes with a great company, camels bearing spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones, and she opens all that is in her heart to him.
Solomon answers every question she brings; nothing is hidden from him that he cannot explain to her.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: When she sees the wisdom of Solomon, the house he built, the food on his table, the order of his servants and their apparel, and his ascent into the house of the Lord, there is no more spirit left in her.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: She confesses that the report she heard in her own land of his acts and wisdom was true.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: She admits she did not believe the words until she came and saw it with her own eyes, and now she declares that not even half the greatness of his wisdom was told to her; he exceeds the fame that reached her.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: She calls his men and servants happy because they stand continually before him and hear his wisdom.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: She blesses the Lord who delighted in Solomon and set him on the throne, and she states plainly that it is because the Most High loved Israel and would establish them forever that he made Solomon king to do judgment and justice.
The wisdom and glory of the king trace back to the God of Israel, not to Solomon alone.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: The queen gives Solomon 120 talents of gold, spices in great abundance, and precious stones; there was never such spice as she brought.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: The servants of Huram and Solomon bring gold from Ophir along with algum trees and precious stones, and the king makes terraces for the house of the Lord and the palace, and harps and psalteries for singers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Solomon gives the queen all she desires beyond what she brought, and she returns to her own land.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: The weight of gold coming to Solomon in one year is six hundred sixty and six talents, beyond what merchants and the kings of Arabia and the governors bring.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Solomon makes two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold and puts them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: The king makes a great throne of ivory overlaid with pure gold, with six steps, a footstool of gold, stays on each side, and lions standing by the stays and on the steps; there was none like it in any kingdom.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: All his drinking vessels and the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon are pure gold, none of silver, because silver was not counted for anything in his days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: His ships go to Tarshish with the servants of Huram and return every three years bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks; consider the amount gathered by a crew laboring three years for one voyage.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Solomon surpasses all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom, and all of them seek his presence to hear the wisdom the Most High put in his heart.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Every man brings his present year by year, vessels of silver and gold, garments, armor, spices, horses, and mules.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Solomon has four thousand stalls for horses and chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, stationed in the chariot cities and at Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: He reigns over all the kings from the river to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt, and he makes silver as plentiful as stones in Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Horses are brought to him out of Egypt and out of all lands.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: The rest of the acts of Solomon are written in the book of Nathan the prophet, the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
After all these great works Solomon dies, and the account turns to his son who is raised up next.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Solomon reigns in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years, then sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and his son Rehoboam reigns in his place.
